summary:
MAGNITUDE QA GATE verified end-to-end. 15/15 pytest cases pass in /app/backend/tests/test_magnitude_gate.py. (1) POST /api/calibration exercises the gate on the user's base photo at drop_pct 5/10/15; the record is persisted with the correct shape: current_body_fat_pct (25.9), 3 renders each with drop_pct, target_body_fat_pct (= current − drop, floored at 3), a stored image path, and a qa object; plus pairwise_distinctness keyed 5vs10/5vs15/10vs15. Directly inspected MongoDB confirms all 3 calibration renders escalated to mode='progressive' with steps=3, expected_visible=true, score_single<0.08 (0.0302, 0.0266, 0.0378) and final score after progressive retry (0.0496, 0.0516, 0.0521) — proving near-copy detection and progressive multi-step re-edit both execute. (2) GET /api/files/{path}?token= returns valid image bytes (PNG or JPEG magic) for all 3 calibration image paths; 401 without a token, 403 for non-owner paths (owner-authorized). (3) POST /api/generate → poll /api/generate/{job_id} completes in ~120s. Returned future_self_set.renders.{conservative,expected,stretch} each includes path, weight_kg, body_fat_pct, what_it_takes, AND a qa object. Backend logs across multiple runs show the stretch label (largest delta) reliably escalating to qa.mode='progressive' (e.g., score_single=0.0259 → 0.0513 after 3 steps) while conservative/expected — whose |Δbf| is <4.0 for this user's plan — correctly report mode='single', expected_visible=false, score=null. No hangs, no 500s in the /generate flow. (4) GET /api/calibration/view?token=<jwt> returns 200 text/html with all 3 image paths embedded; 401 with a garbage token; 422 when the token query param is omitted (FastAPI required-query behavior — acceptable rejection).

BACKEND USABILITY FINDING (HIGH): POST /api/calibration reliably exceeds the Cloudflare edge's hard 60s response timeout, so real clients receive a 502 (verified: `time=60.095s HTTP=502` on raw curl). The backend does finish and persist the record ~90–160s later, so /view + /files subsequently work — but a mobile client cannot read the JSON response (with the qa metadata / pairwise_distinctness) directly. Recommend converting /api/calibration to the same async-job pattern already used for /api/generate (start → poll), or run the three drops concurrently with asyncio.gather like _run_generation already does.

critical.issue: Synchronous request that reliably exceeds the Cloudflare 60s edge timeout — returns 502 to clients (verified via raw curl and pytest). Backend completes ~90-160s later so persisted data is fine, but the JSON body containing qa/pairwise_distinctness is unreachable to any client. Fix: convert to async job (like /api/generate) or run the 3 drops concurrently with asyncio.gather (each drop already retries internally).

minor.issue: img_bytes returned by the AI provider are sometimes JPEG (magic 0xFF D8 FF) but the object is always stored/served with content-type 'image/png' and a '.png' path suffix (server.py:344, 428). Browsers still render OK, but content-type is misreported; consider sniffing the magic bytes and setting the correct mime + extension.

One run observed a 500 from server.py:424 with 'Image model returned no image after retries. I cannot edit the image as requested.' — Gemini refused the edit and the whole calibration aborts. Since the gate already retries per-image internally, consider catching provider RuntimeError per-drop and continuing with the remaining drops (partial success + qa.error field) instead of failing the entire request.

test_report_links: /app/backend/tests/test_magnitude_gate.py — new pytest suite, 15 cases (calibration persistence + files endpoint + calibration/view HTML + /generate flow with qa)
action_items: HIGH: Refactor POST /api/calibration to be non-blocking. Either (a) run the 3 drops with asyncio.gather (mirrors _run_generation) so total wall clock drops to ~one drop's worth (~30-60s, under the 60s edge cap most of the time), or (b) return a job_id and expose GET /api/calibration/{job_id} to poll — same pattern already implemented for /api/generate. Right now real clients cannot read the calibration JSON response through the public URL.

MINOR: Detect JPEG vs PNG magic in server.py at the objstore.put_object call sites (line 344 in _run_generation and line 428 in calibration) and set the correct content-type + file extension. Currently everything is force-labeled '.png' / 'image/png'.
MINOR: Wrap each per-drop render in calibration() in a try/except so a Gemini refusal on one drop does not 500 the entire calibration; record qa.error on that drop and continue.
critical_code_review_comments: image_qa.change_score: contrast-normalized 96x96 grayscale MAD is a sensible framing-level metric; near-copy threshold 0.08 aligns with observed score_single values (0.023-0.038 for near-copies vs 0.05+ after progressive escalation). Divide-by-zero guarded with +1e-6. Exception path returns 1.0 (fail-open on decode errors) which is the right default.

ai_provider.render_with_magnitude_gate: correctly short-circuits with mode='single', expected_visible=False, score=None when |Δbf| < VISIBLE_THRESHOLD_BF (4.0). When expected_visible=True AND score < NEAR_COPY_MAX (0.08), it runs 3 progressive steps feeding each output as the next input — exactly the spec. Records both score_single and final score in qa. Session IDs are namespaced per-step ('{session_id}-step{k}').
server._run_generation: uses asyncio.gather across the three targets — good. Stores qa in future_self_set.renders.<label>.qa. Logs each render's qa (verified in backend logs).

server.calibration: THREE renders run SEQUENTIALLY inside a for-loop (server.py:422-430). That's what pushes total wall clock past the 60s Cloudflare cap. Trivially parallelizable via asyncio.gather like _run_generation already does.

server.serve_file + server.calibration_view: token-in-query auth path is correct (bearer header can't be sent by ), owner check via path prefix is enforced, unknown/garbage tokens produce 401. No ObjectId leakage — endpoints pipe through _clean() where needed.
server._resolve_user_from_token swallows all JWT decode exceptions and returns None → 401. Correct.

success_rate.frontend: not tested (backend-only scope per review request)

seed_data_creation: None — reused the provided account e2e1788128321@trueform.app / Test1234! which already has base_photo + completed onboarding. The tests write one new calibration record + one new future_self_set per run (overwritten by upsert, no accumulation).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Magnitude QA gate is green as of iteration_4. Test file to reuse: /app/backend/tests/test_magnitude_gate.py (15 cases, xdist-safe with loadscope, uses fixtures at module scope). Key handling: POST /api/calibration will 502 through the public URL because Cloudflare caps responses at 60s and the endpoint is sequential (~90-160s); the tests work around this by polling GET /api/calibration/view for HTML persistence and reading paths from there — DO NOT retighten those into strict 200-on-POST assertions until the endpoint is refactored to async-job or asyncio.gather. Fresh calibration runs may occasionally 500 if Gemini's safety filter refuses one drop; the tests tolerate this and re-check persistence from a prior run. Same JPEG-vs-PNG mime mismatch applies to /api/files output — accept both magic sequences.
rca_of_issue: Root cause of the 502 on POST /api/calibration is architectural, not a bug in the magnitude gate itself: server.py:422-430 iterates drop_pct in (5,10,15) SEQUENTIALLY, each call taking ~20-50s (progressive path adds 3 extra image calls). Total wall clock exceeds the CF edge's 60s response cap → 502 to the client, though asyncio-suspended backend keeps going and finally upserts the calibrations document, which is why /view and /files subsequently succeed. Mitigation options ranked: (1) `results = await asyncio.gather(*[_one_drop(d) for d in (5,10,15)])` — same shape as _run_generation already uses; likely brings the endpoint under 60s in the common case. (2) Convert to a background job with a job_id, mirror /api/generate. Progressive-retry logic itself is working correctly (verified via Mongo dump of the calibration doc showing mode='progressive' with valid score_single/score/steps for all 3 drops).
